correctness.rationale: The two-term uniqueness theorem gives the exact marked-leader identity |V(S)|=3M(S). Each admissible branch parameter has two torus lifts, while at most twelve marked summands can lie above the branch exceptional set. Combining this with the source character-sum bounds gives the stated uniform q/6+O(sqrt(q)) estimate. The q=9 exhaustive check agrees with the theorem.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2026 source paper establishes coset weights and constructs one leader but does not state all-leader multiplicities; the 1986 source treats quasi-perfectness and ordinary weight spectra. Searches found no matching theorem. Two older decoding references were not inspected at theorem level and remain explicit residual risks, as does the extreme recency of the motivating preprint.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a one-leader construction into a uniform quantitative theorem for every farthest coset, with square-root discrepancy and an exact norm-orbit invariance that reduces future exact classification to syndrome norm classes.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
